findings.title: Invalidate calendar status after deleting the cache
findings.body: A successful cache deletion only shows a toast and invokes the optional onSuccess callback. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper allows that callback to be omitted and does not invalidate its connectedCalendars query itself. Consequently, the dropdown continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action after reporting success; window-focus refetching is also disabled. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve persisted cache records for delegated connections
findings.body: Connected calendars can contain in-memory delegation credentials, but CalendarCache rows reference persisted credential IDs. The existing availability reader explicitly handles this by looking up delegated cache entries using userId and key. Querying status only by the connected credential ID therefore returns no status for those delegated accounts even when they are actively serving cached availability. Since their regular connection is hidden and they cannot be disconnected, the dropdown disappears entirely, leaving no way to inspect or clear that cache. Resolve the underlying persisted cache records and a valid deletion target for delegated connections.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory. Running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root writes to `.env` in the repository's parent directory rather than the root environment file used by the application. The script reports success while CalendarService continues using the old webhook URL. Derive the repository root from the script's location before constructing this path.

findings.title: Make the environment update work with GNU sed
findings.body: The `sed -i ''` syntax is specific to BSD/macOS sed. With GNU sed, updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL fails and leaves its value unchanged. Because the exit status is ignored, the script still announces that the new tunnel URL was installed, so subsequent calendar subscriptions use the stale endpoint. Use a portable replacement strategy or handle the platform-specific sed syntax and check for failure.
